_notes: Scaled setup: solvers are scored on the 73 Maros-Meszaros problems the reproduced Python solver can hold as dense arrays (n <= 1000, dense data <= 2 GB), split 37 train / 36 test, under an evaluator-enforced 120 CPU-second budget per instance. The held-out test uses evaluator-generated perturbations of its problems (two hidden draws each) and a hidden family of 36 generated degenerate QPs. Success is decided by the evaluator's own KKT check of the returned primal-dual point, never by solver-reported status. Paper values the gym cannot match on its scale are kept under '_paper_results'; see each experiment's _setup_note. Success is the paper's stopping test (Eq. 52, absolute = relative tolerance) recomputed by the evaluator from the returned point, plus a sqrt(eps) relative duality-gap guard. Coefficients are magnitudes; direction comes from higher_is_better.

failure_rate_comparison.description: Failure rate on Maros-Meszaros QPs at medium (1e-6) and high (1e-9) requested accuracy (paper Table III). Every instance of the fixed manifest is in the denominator; an instance is solved only if the evaluator verifies the returned (x, y, z).

failure_rate_medium.description: Percentage of manifest instances without a verified 1e-6 solution (missing, crashed, over budget, or failing the KKT check).

failure_rate_high.description: Percentage of manifest instances without a verified 1e-9 solution; catches methods that only work at loose tolerances.

failure_rate_comparison._setup_note: Not on the paper's scale. The paper's Table III values (C++ ODYN, 103-problem subset, 120 s wall-clock limit, solver-reported convergence) are kept under _paper_results: ODYN 9.7 / 15.5 %, OSQP 44.7 / 49.5 % at medium / high. 'results' holds this gym's paper-level reproduction (scoring/scores.json: the 73 tractable problems unperturbed, Python reference, 120 CPU-s budget, evaluator-verified Eq. 52 + gap guard), where the reference fails about twice as often as the paper's C++ solver while the ODYN-vs-OSQP gap of the paper reproduces (20.5 vs 41.1 % medium). The ranked comparison uses scoring/scores_test.json, not these numbers.

degenerate_problems.description: Failure rate on degenerate QPs (redundant active inequalities, LICQ failure with rank-deficient and badly scaled data, positive-semidefinite Hessians with non-unique solutions) at medium and high accuracy (paper Table IV categories).

degenerate_failure_rate_medium.description: Percentage of degenerate instances without a verified 1e-6 solution.

degenerate_failure_rate_high.description: Percentage of degenerate instances without a verified 1e-9 solution.

degenerate_problems._setup_note: Paper values are derived from Table IV: the share of its three degenerate problems a solver did not solve (OSQP declared the LICQ-failure problem dual infeasible; every other solver solved all three; the accuracy setting is not stated, so the same derived value is entered at both accuracies). The paper reports iteration counts, which the gym does not score because a method's own iteration count cannot be verified. The gym scores the paper's three problems (train / paper-level) and a generated family of the same three categories (12 instances each, n in {8, 16, 32, 64}; the test family uses a hidden seed). High accuracy is the primary metric and carries the larger coefficient: at 1e-6 the generated family barely separates solvers (train: reference and baseline both fail 2 of 39), while 1e-9 exposes the numerical fragility the paper's degenerate-problem study is about (test: reference 8.3 %, OSQP 33.3 %).
